body:
Review RCOURS of https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/pull/6 reproduced that a short response could enter the shared artifact cache and break later builds. The user requested this round to “fix review RCOURS2's findings” after the fresh review found two added regressions and five inherited download problems: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/tree/wip/RCOURS2-evidence-20261023.

Response bytes are now checked before decoding and before the temporary file is promoted into the cache. Fixed-length reads stay within their declared framing; range counts are also checked against actual response bytes, and chunked responses must consume their closing chunk even after the range count or decoder reaches its ending. Mixed-case range units are accepted. Gzip and deflate coding names are case-insensitive, supported stacked codings decode in reverse order, and unsupported codings are rejected. Encoded partial responses cannot append to a saved decoded prefix.

No-body responses, including an unsolicited 304 to an unconditional GET, cannot publish an artifact. Body-bearing successful statuses and unfollowed redirect bodies remain accepted, and existing HTTP error reporting remains intact. Every rejected download removes its temporary bytes before releasing ownership. Uncompressed close-delimited bodies retain progress between fragments; only decoder lookahead probes for the framing end. Encoding errors are limited to decoder operations; file-output and response-framing errors retain their own cause and full values.

Main remains at https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/commit/f7ac8c67dbe757d9129cfa453a37f2867bd1272d, which contains the earlier buffer-sizing change. It does not supersede this PR's length/range validation or this round's framing/encoding fixes.

Validation (all local, real loopback HTTP servers and isolated cache directories):

- A1–A7 fail on the original 7ab7bfff implementation in single attempts; both A5 stream-cleanup cases fail independently. Initial boundary register: 6 pass / 18 fail in 24 attempts. Expanded original-implementation register plus buffer suite: 20 pass / 27 fail in 47 attempts.
- Independent review found a valid 203 rejection and output I/O mislabeled as encoding errors: both fail first, then pass after correction. The portable full native-output-error assertion also fails with the broad encoding catch restored (34 pass / 1 fail in 35 first attempts).
- All 38 new framing scenarios, 43 length scenarios and 14 buffer scenarios pass 30/30: 95 cases per round, 2,850 first attempts, zero retries, failures, errors or skips on [head ac74fa03a](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/commit/ac74fa03ab018e66a67f293dbae7a4fe3a7bd367).
- Complete JVM cache module: 187/187 first attempts, zero retries, errors, failures or skips, under the shared memory slot on the same head. The earlier 183/186 run is retained below as regression evidence, not counted as a clean gate.
- The first module gate exposed three unchanged redirect tests rejected by the initial status guard (183 pass / 3 fail in 186 first attempts). A new real-server case reproduced the same class across 301, 302, 303, 307 and 308; the targeted register flipped from 101 pass / 4 fail to 105/105. The guard now rejects only informational responses, 204, 205 and 304.
- Compatibility checks additionally reproduce and fix the exact existing 500-error text and progress for a close-delimited body held between fragments; the unchanged location-ownership error test also flips from failing to passing (targeted register 37 pass / 3 fail before, 40/40 after).
- All six RCOURS2 coverage groups are closed: range-unit case; chunked range endings/excess bytes; no-body status/HEAD metadata; other/mixed-case codings; real stream-error cleanup; concurrent same-file callers during rejection and ownership release.
- Independent test-coverage and code-review passes are saved with the evidence. The native file-error assertion uses a real failing filesystem open to obtain the complete platform error, with no platform skip or substring assertion.

Existing-test change inventory for this round: `DownloadBufferCapacityTests.scala` changes only “other content encodings retain the default maximum” to “deflate content encoding retains the default maximum.” Before: three uncompressed bytes advertised as the unsupported `custom` coding, with raw bytes expected. After: a real deflate stream, with decoded bytes expected; all maximum-buffer, exact configured-buffer observation, stream-close and body assertions remain. This corrects a test that expected unknown codings to be cached; the changed assertion fails with the original implementation. No other existing test body, assertion, timeout or iteration count changed. The previous round's standalone zero-byte-read case remains intact. No diagnostic golden literals changed.

Within the new framing suite, the no-body error expectation changed from “expected 200 or 206 with an artifact body” to “expected a response with an artifact body,” matching body-bearing 2xx and unfollowed redirect compatibility. Its new output-error assertion changed from Linux's literal native exception to the complete native error from the same filesystem operation; the restored-bug run above proves it still catches the encoding-label error. No reflection, mocks, visibility increases for tests, disabled tests, timeout increases, iteration reductions or retry wrappers were introduced.

This round's sources, patches, XML, exact attempt audits, reviews and checkpoints: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/tree/wip/FCOURS4-evidence-20261023 . Earlier-round evidence remains at https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/coursier/tree/wip/FCOURS2-evidence-20261022 . CI is left to the campaign orchestrator as requested. The PR remains open for review.
